## Introduction

4/24/20 Los Alamos National Laboratory

• BaF2 is one of the fastest known scintillators, emitting at 220 nm with

sub-nanosecond decay constant [2] – Excellent for timing applications • 4.88 g/cm3 à High detection efficiency

– At 15 cm thick, nearly 100% efficient for gammas up to 10 MeV [3] • Problem: ~80% of the total light output consists of slower (600 ns

decay constant) emission peaked at 310 nm [2] – High count rate à pile up • Goal: develop a BaF2-based detector that leverages the fast emission

component for optimal timing characteristics – Suppression of slow component

2

## Farukhi (1971)

4/24/20 Los Alamos National Laboratory

• First to discover BaF2 scintillation • BaF2 grown at Harshaw; “clarity and transmittance from VUV to IR”

– Chubb (1956 letter to editor): Low wavelength transmission cutoff at 134.5nm; “useful new optical

material for vacuum ultraviolet, non-hydroscopic, very slightly water soluble” • 8-10% of NaI pulse height • 630 ns decay time (average) • Found UV band @ 325nm and red band at 625nm • IOR of 1.495 @ 325nm • Dopants either suppress (slow) scintillation or make no difference à scintillation

inherent to host lattice • Mechanism not well understood

– Analogy to unactivated alkali halides (NaI): exciton decay and I- ion, tendency of holes to be self-

trapped at halogen ions (Physics of Color centers)

– Tzalmona and Pershan: two types of BaF hole centers – Theory: scintillation associated with modification of hole centers

42

## Laval (1982)

4/24/20 Los Alamos National Laboratory

• First to discover fast component of BaF2 scintillation • Notes the need for fast, high density scintillators for time-of-flight PET • Measured emission spectrum via X-ray excitation and a monochromator

– main emission peak at 310nm, smaller peak at 220nm • Measured pulse shape using single photon counting, found fast and slow components

– Fast: 550ps fwhm, 600ps/790ps decay constants

– Slow: 430ns/620ns decay constants • Measured time-resolved emission spectrum using single photon counting with
